sanskrit_verse:
दूराद् उच्छिष्टविण्मूत्रपादाम्भांसि समुत्सृजेत् ।
श्रुतिस्मृत्युदितं सम्यङ् नित्यम् आचारम् आचरेत् ॥१५४॥
transliteration: dūrād ucchiṣṭaviṇmūtrapādāmbhāṃsi samutsṛjet | śrutismṛtyuditaṃ samyaṅ nityam ācāram ācaret || 1.154 ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One must release excreta, urine, leftover food, and washing water at a distance, and always conduct oneself according to the injunctions declared in Shruti and Smriti.

Restoration logic depends on maintaining ritual and ethical cleanliness
Consciousness alignment occurs through adherence to codified dharma

IF agent fails to follow Shruti-Smriti directives THEN invoke consciousness recalibration through supervised conduct repetition

IF habitual neglect observed THEN activate capacity-building regimen under qualified supervision
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes threshold norms for personal hygiene and scriptural compliance as prerequisites for legal standing. Violations indicate diminished capacity rather than culpability, necessitating restoration-based judicial interventions aligned with Vedic order.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality locates impurity not in intent but in misalignment with śruti-smṛti-sanctioned action sequences. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that improper disposal leads to sequential disorder in individual and societal harmony. Responsibility is proportional to knowledge-access; correction restores causal integrity without punitive overlay.
